title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic kidney disease and diabetes.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of chronic kidney disease stage 4 and type 2 diabetes. The patient reports feeling stable overall. He continues to manage his blood glucose levels through diet and exercise alone, and he is not currently taking any medications for his glucose management. He notes that his kidney function has remained steady over the last six months. He denies any acute symptoms or new concerns regarding his renal status.

Medication List
None for diabetes.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Vital signs are stable. Physical examination shows no acute distress. Skin is intact with no new lesions. No edema noted in lower extremities.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Currently diet controlled.
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: This condition is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current lifestyle modifications. The patient will maintain his current nutritional plan and exercise routine. Follow up in three months for a repeat laboratory evaluation of renal function.
explanations: The provider states the CKD is not due to diabetes, so the presumed link does not apply: code diabetes without complications and CKD separately.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.

distractors.why: The 'with' presumption is overridden when the provider documents another cause or no link.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
